chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said:
Verily, upon every truth there is a reality, and upon every right action there is a light. So take whatever agrees with the Book of God, and leave whatever contradicts the Book of God.

key_terms.حق: Truth, right, divine claim — here referring to a claim or statement presented as true
key_terms.حقيقة: Reality, essence, the inner truth behind an outward claim
key_terms.صواب: Correctness, right action, that which is sound and proper
key_terms.كتاب الله: The Book of God — the Quran as the supreme criterion and authority
key_terms.نور: Light — metaphor for clarity, guidance, and divine illumination

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about testing hadith against the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) presents the Quran as the ultimate criterion for evaluating hadith and teachings: every truth has an underlying reality, and every correct statement carries light, and the standard to determine this is conformity with the Book of God. This teaching, transmitted through the Imams of the Ahlulbayt to al-Saduq's gathering in 368 AH, reflects the Shia principle of using the Quran to authenticate hadith and reject fabrications.
